title: Model affinity and selector resolution for SDK: tag, semver, commit-hash, and floating refs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define deterministic, observable semantics for resolving model selectors delivered via SDK/API. Support three primary selector types (tag, semver, commit-hash) plus floating refs (eg. 'latest', 'stable') and ensure clear precedence, caching, and telemetry so customers can rely on stable behaviour during rollouts and incidents.
background: We onboard new model variants frequently and customers request pinning by human-friendly labels (tags), semver ranges, and immutable commit hashes. Current SDK behavior is underspecified: tags are treated like mutable labels in some places but cached aggressively, semver is not supported consistently, and commit-hash resolution sometimes falls back unexpectedly to other variants. This causes customer confusion during rollouts and complicates caching and telemetry mapping.
decision_log: Use commit-hash (exact SHA) as ultimate ground-truth selector: resolves only to exact artifact; no fallbacks permitted.
Support semver selectors with two modes: exact-match (eg '1.2.3') and prefix/range (eg '1.x' or '^1.2.0'). Semver ranges will resolve to the highest compatible published release at resolution time.

Treat tag selectors as mutable symbolic refs. Tags resolve to the model version currently pointed to by the tag at resolution time. Tag resolution emits a 'tag_resolved_to' telemetry field containing the resolved version.

Introduce 'floating refs' reserved keywords: 'latest' resolves to latest stable semver-major.minor.patch (non-prerelease) and 'stable' maps to the version with the 'stable' tag in the same repository. These are convenience selectors but considered mutable and may be rate-limited to reduce unexpected behavior.

Precedence order when multiple selectors are provided: explicit commit-hash > semver exact/range > tag > floating ref. If multiple selectors are present and conflict, SDK returns a 409 conflict with resolution details unless client passes 'resolveStrategy=preferFirst' (opt-in).

Cache semantics: client SDK will cache resolved mapping for tag/semver/floating refs for a configurable TTL (default 60s). Commit-hash never cached as a mapping because it is immutable. TTL changes require release-level rollout and are exposed as a config parameter in SDK.
Fallback rules: only allowed when selector is semver range and no matching published release exists — in that case, return 404 with helpful message. No automatic fallback to other model families.
Telemetry: emit resolution event with selector_type, selector_value, resolved_version, resolution_time_ms, resolution_source (cache|control_plane|catalog), and cache_ttl_used.

Backward compatibility: existing SDKs that pass raw 'model' strings will be interpreted under the new resolver using heuristics (SHA-like strings = commit-hash, semver-like strings parsed as semver, otherwise tag). We will warn in logs for ambiguous selectors and encourage explicit selector typing in DTOs.
api_changes: New parameter on model selection API and SDK: model_selector { type: 'commit'|'semver'|'tag'|'floating', value: string } (SDK will provide helpers); server accepts legacy 'model' string for backward compat.
New query param 'resolveStrategy' with values 'strict' (default) | 'preferFirst' to control conflict behavior.
HTTP 409 returned when multiple selectors conflict under 'strict' mode. Response includes 'resolved_candidates' array and 'recommended_selector' string.
Examples to document in SDK readme: commit selector -> 'commit:1a2b3c4d', semver prefix -> 'semver:^1.2.0', tag -> 'tag:gpu-optimized', floating -> 'floating:latest'.
SDK helpers will include ModelSelector.fromCommit(sha), fromSemverRange(range), fromTag(tag), fromFloating(ref).
Server will add 'X-Resolved-Model' response header with final version ref for easier tracing in edge logs.
runtime_behavior: Resolution happens at the edge proxy if a valid cache entry exists, otherwise the control plane catalog is queried. Resolved mappings for tag/semver/floating are cached in an in-memory LRU with TTL and persisted to Redis for cross-instance consistency. Commit-hash skips mapping and is validated against the artifact catalog for existence. During routing, runtime attaches the canonical model version id to the container allocation request to prevent mismatched binaries.
acceptance_criteria: Given an exact commit selector, requests always route to the artifact with that commit and 0% variance in resolution across repeated requests.
Given a semver range, control plane resolves to highest compatible published version and returns identical resolved_version within resolution TTL window.
Tag resolution returns the version currently pointed to and includes telemetry fields; resolving identical tag repeatedly within TTL uses cache and emits cache_ttl_used>0.
SDK exposes ModelSelector helpers and unit tests cover parsing heuristics and serialization.
Telemetry events are emitted and visible in console dashboard and include resolution_source and resolved_version.
409 conflict behavior exercised in integration tests when multiple selectors disagree and 'strict' is used; 'preferFirst' path exercised and documented.
No automatic fallback from commit-hash to other selectors; attempts are rejected with 400/404 semantics when artifact missing.
E2E load test with tag-to-version rollouts demonstrates cache TTL behavior and does not materially impact P50 latency (<= 5ms added at resolution stage under typical conditions).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): SDK + control-plane resolver change deployed to staging. Enable detailed telemetry. Duration: 1 week.
Phase 2 (limited production): Enable for 10% of traffic via rollout rule; monitor resolved_version stability, error rates, and SLOs for model route. Duration: 2 weeks.
Phase 3 (general): Gradually increase to 100% and flip default TTL to 60s in SDK agents. Announce migration guide to customers and partners.
Rollback: revert SDK default to legacy heuristics and disable mapping cache persistence; control-plane toggles revert to previous resolver implementation.
migration_notes: Customers using free-text model strings will continue to work but should migrate to explicit ModelSelector helpers to avoid ambiguity.
Recommend pinning by commit-hash for production-critical flows where immutability is required.
For progressive rollouts, recommend semver ranges with canary releases and short tag TTLs to accelerate switch-over while preserving observability.
Document examples for converting existing 'model: "gpt-4x"' strings to explicit selectors with minimal code changes.
test_plan: Unit tests for selector parsing and precedence rules.
Integration tests exercising cache hits and misses for tag/semver/floating refs across multiple instances.
Chaos test that simulates tag retargeting during TTL window to ensure cache semantics and telemetry reflect the transient inconsistency.
Load test verifying resolution latency at P50/P95 under typical production traffic patterns.
Cross-SDK compatibility test matrix (python/js/go) to ensure SDK helper serialization matches server expectations.
open_questions: What default TTL should we pick for customers who do not configure SDK? Proposal: 60s default with platform override per-tenant.
Should we allow configurable fallback chains (eg semver->tag) for advanced customers? Proposal: not in initial release; consider as opt-in extension later.
How aggressively should we surface ambiguous selector warnings in logs vs breaking behavior? Current plan: warn by default, fail in 'strict' mode.
Do we require an audit trail in the control plane showing tag retargeting history for compliance customers? Proposal: yes, add 'tag_retarg_history' in a later ticket.
